title: SLO-Mediated Microbatch Suspension with Predictive KV Warmup and Memory Defragmentation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement an SLO-aware microbatch suspension mechanism that proactively checkpoints lightweight KV slices before suspending in-flight microbatches, opportunistically performs a compacting GPU memory pass, and resumes with predictive KV warmup to avoid SLO regressions.

Motivation: continuous batching yields high throughput but suffers tail-latency spikes when preemption forces KV cache eviction or when fragmented GPU memory prevents efficient resumption. Current preemption is a blunt interrupt: it either allows batches to finish (increasing latency) or kills them (causing work loss and cold KV misses). We need a middle ground that protects latency SLOs, preserves fairness across tenants, and reduces repeated cold-warm cycles for KV state.

Proposed approach (high-level):
- SLO bucketing: categorize requests into latency buckets (e.g., strict 50ms, nominal 200ms, best-effort) using route metadata and recent SLA telemetry.
- Microbatch suspension: allow in-progress microbatches to be suspended at natural yield points (end of token generation window). At suspension, record a compact checkpoint that contains minimal KV slice metadata (keys, compressed small summary) to disk or pinned host-memory.
- Predictive KV warmup: when scheduling a suspended microbatch for resumption, prefetch the small checkpointed KV slice and apply a lightweight warmup pass to reconstruct the most-likely working set before allocating GPU KV pages.
- Opportunistic compaction: when a tenant's memory pressure triggers preemption, run a short, space-efficient GPU memory compaction/defragmentation pass targeted at freed KV slots to reduce fragmentation and increase reuse without a full eviction.
- Hysteresis windows and fairness: introduce tenant-specific hysteresis windows (configurable per SLA tier) to avoid ping-pong suspend/resume. Use a credit-like fairness ledger so long-running tenants don't monopolize compaction cycles. Credits earn back gradually for low-impact tenants.

Key constraints and trade-offs:
- Checkpoint size vs. resume latency: smaller checkpoints reduce I/O but may increase the number of warm misses on resume; choose adaptive checkpoint granularity based on token budget and sequence-length distribution.
- Compaction CPU/GPU cost: compaction consumes cycles; make it opportunistic and rate-limited to avoid harming high-priority latency requests.
- Prediction accuracy: warmup effectiveness depends on prediction heuristics; we will start with simple recency-based heuristics and evaluate on production traces before iterating.

Success criteria (MVP):
- 30% reduction in tail-latency spikes (>95th percentile) for routes with mixed SLOs during high contention windows (measured on synthetic and 2 production tenants).
- No more than 5% throughput regression for P0 routes after enabling suspension & warmup.
- Demonstrated GPU memory fragmentation reduction (measured by reclaimed contiguous pages) after compaction pass in controlled tests.

Deliverables:
- Design doc with API changes for suspend/resume and checkpoint format (Confluence).
- Runtime implemention: checkpointing, warmup prefetch, compacting pass, hysteresis/credits, and metrics.
- Integration tests and a load-test dashboard.
- Canary rollout plan with automatic rollback if P0 latency increases beyond 2x baseline.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after spike analysis on 2026-02-27 showed repeated cold KV misses during preemption events. Linked traces and latency heatmaps in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Suspend-Resume-Design

2026-03-03 - Marco Ruiz: Spike-safe prototype for 'checkpoint metadata' serialized to host-pinned region is passing unit tests. Initial format includes: tenant_id, batch_id, top-32 keys (hashed), and compacted token offsets. Pushing draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2146

2026-03-04 - Review (Yvonne Chen - infra): Concern about increasing host memory footprint for pinned checkpoints. Decision: keep per-checkpoint budget < 16KB by default, add eviction TTL, and expose per-tenant knob in Dedicated configs.

2026-03-05 - Marco Ruiz: Implemented predictive warmup using recency + token-frequency scoring. Local perf: resume latency improved median by 18% and tail by 24% on recorded traces (replay harness). Draft PR updated: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2146 (WIP)

2026-03-07 - Design review (Product - Lina Gomez): Align SLO bucketing vocabulary with Console routing metadata. Action: PM to add route-level 'latency_tier' field and map to warmup aggressiveness. Added to console-2026.02 planning doc.

2026-03-08 - Eng sync: Added opportunistic compaction that runs only when freed_slots_ratio > 12% and there are suspended microbatches. Compaction implemented as two-phase: quick defragment (on-GPU pointer remap) followed by deferred full compact. Measure impact first on canary fleet.

2026-03-09 - QA (Jordan Lee): Added integration tests for suspend/resume under preemption and simulated KV churn. Found race where a resumed microbatch could start while its checkpoint eviction TTL lapsed; fix in next patch: bump TTL to 60s and add atomic reservation. Test dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/d/kv-warmup/canary-compare

2026-03-10 - Security review note (Sasha Ivanov): No customer data is persisted in the checkpoint; keys are hashed and compressed. Confirmed compliance with on-prem deployment data rules. No additional KMS changes required for MVP.
